data.title: From 9/11 to burn pits, we must deal with long-term effects of toxic exposure
data.description:
Two days after 9/11 my buddy and I took a bus from our hometown in Clifton, N.J., and went into Manhattan. We wandered around the city and made our way south to what would later be called Ground Zero.

There were three things from that day that are seared into my memory. The first was the families of victims at the Manhattan Armory, carrying pictures of loved ones begging people to help them find their missing family and friends. The second was the smell. It was a combination of smoke, concrete, chemicals and batteries. The third was how bad it felt to breathe. I was a smoker at the time and told my buddy when we were making our way home that I felt like I just smoked a carton of cigarettes.

Years later, in Iraq, I had the ignominious duty of burning everything that was trash every single night. We burned everything to the point that it made zero sense. I was told that we didn’t want our trash to be sifted through by the enemy, so we had to burn everything. Plastic bottles, computers, batteries, paper, and all trash. When you dared ask if it was necessary or safe, you got chewed out.

In 2011, I was at the VA in San Diego to ask about a bump in my throat. The doctors found a lump on my thyroid. I asked if it had anything to do with my exposure to burn pits. They laughed at me and said no.

A couple of years later, the lump had doubled in size and had to be removed, along with half my thyroid. They had to conduct a sleep test before I could do surgery and found I had sleep apnea. I asked again if this and the growth had anything to do with exposure and was told no.

Around the same time, the brave men and women who worked around the clock at Ground Zero started coming down with similar yet more severe symptoms. They developed respiratory issues such as coughs, wheezing, shortness of breath and asthma. They would have sinus issues and reflux from their airways into the lungs. And some got cancer. Respiratory, blood, and lymph node cancers became prevalent.

Twenty-five years since the terror attacks on the U.S., and 25 years into what we labeled a “war on terror,” we have to come to terms with the fact that long term care for both 9/11 responders and Global War on Terrorism veterans is way more complex that what we thought it would be. We also knew but chose to ignore the fact that exposure would lead to long term effects.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani made news when he said that city officials at the time knew the air quality was bad but misled people by claiming it was safe. Of course, in the world we live in people couldn’t understand why he decided to come out and talk about this, calling it some type of conspiracy theory.

There is no conspiracy. The federal, state and local authorities knew there was asbestos, chemicals and toxins in the air. They said it was safe, based on regulations at the time. But they didn’t or wouldn’t factor in long term effects. It might be safe to be at Ground Zero for a day, like I was. But repeated days that went on for months? Surely, they had to know that wasn’t safe.

It was not a fair position to be in. Then-Mayor Rudy Guiliani had to get the city back to a sense of normalcy. New York isn’t just a normal run-of-the-mill city. It was and is the financial capital of the world. The clean up efforts had to happen as fast as possible.

That means there were hard decisions to be made. Yes, you had to look at the short-term needs which were very urgent. But leadership also means balancing the short-term needs with the long-term effects. And that is where the government failed us. Millions of dollars have been paid out to 9/11 responders, even though it has taken herculean efforts from advocates like Jon Stewart. And veterans are now getting help for their own exposure to burn pits, thanks to the PACT Act.

Despite this, there is still work to be done. Long term exposure is complex and we still don’t know how bad things will get. Countless more are starting to get symptoms as they get older. We know this because the same thing happened to Vietnam veterans when they were exposed to Agent Orange or Gulf War veterans when they had to breathe in smoke from oil well fires set by Saddam Hussein. The facts show this will be an ongoing issue. Last year, over 10,000 people were diagnosed with 9/11-related cancers.

Mamdani’s release of documents about air quality was needed. We must always look out for the long-term effects even when confronted with an urgent situation. And prepare for the long-term effects, including the financial needs of those who need help. We owe it to them to seek out the truth and advocate for their continued care, no matter the cost.

Joslin Joseph is a recipient of the Military Reporters and Editors award for Best Commentary-Opinion. A graduate of Harvard and Ohio State, he is a Marine veteran who served in Iraq. He currently lives in Anaheim, Calif.

data.title: Yankee Stadium listed in Legionnaires cluster: Officials
data.description:
NEW YORK CITY (WPIX) —  A cooling tower at Yankee Stadium is among 10 towers that tested positive for Legionella bacteria on Sunday as officials investigate an outbreak in the South Bronx.

The New York City Department of Health said all cooling towers that tested positive for Legionella have been ordered to be cleaned and disinfected by Monday.

Officials said polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing can detect the presence of Legionella but cannot show whether the bacteria are alive and does not confirm a cooling tower as the source of exposure. They also reiterated that only live Legionella can cause illness.

Officials urged anyone who lives, works or has visited the affected area since late August and develops flu‑like symptoms to contact a health care provider immediately.

They also said it is safe to shower, drink tap water and use air conditioners in the affected ZIP codes. Officials noted there is no additional risk from being inside any of the 10 buildings.

There will be an in-person town hall for residents to sit down with public health officials on Tuesday at 6 p.m at Metropolitan College in the Bronx.

One person has died in connection with the South Bronx outbreak, and five cases have been confirmed, according to officials.

On the Upper East Side, a Legionnaires’ cluster claimed nine lives and led to more than 90 confirmed cases, with the outbreak first reported at the beginning of July.

Yankee Stadium released the following statement on Sunday night:

In 2024, the Yankees installed new, state-of-the-art, high-efficiency chiller towers at Yankee Stadium, which have undergone water quality and bacteriological indicator testing on a weekly basis over the last three years.

In accordance with DOH regulations, Yankee Stadium provides these results to the DOH on a monthly basis. In the most recent monthly testing on Aug. 20, which was provided to the Department of Health, results were negative for Legionella bacteria. Subsequent to that test, weekly water quality and bacteriological indicator testing was performed on Aug. 26, Sept. 2 and Sept. 9.

Due to the recent community cluster of Legionella bacteria in the Melrose and Morrisania areas of the Bronx (zip codes 10451 and 10456) last week, the NYC Dept. of Health conducted 24 PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) tests of cooling towers in the area, including one at Yankee Stadium on Sept. 11. Yankee Stadium tested positive for trace amounts of Legionella bacteria and was one of 10 cooling towers in the Bronx that tested positive.

A PCR test, which is different from the independent monthly testing Yankee Stadium regularly undertakes, can detect the presence of Legionella bacteria DNA but cannot determine whether the bacteria are alive or dead and does not confirm that a cooling tower is the source of exposure. Only live Legionella bacteria can cause illness.

No current cases have been associated with Yankee Stadium. Additionally, the New York City Department of Health has not at any point this month asked us to postpone our games.

The Health Department is now conducting culture testing to determine whether live Legionella bacteria were present when the samples were collected. Culture results can take up to two weeks.

To reduce the risk of ongoing exposure while culture testing continues, the Health Department mandated that all cooling towers with a positive PCR result conduct a full hyperhalogenation, including draining, cleaning, and disinfection.

Immediate action was taken, and this was completed at Yankee Stadium earlier this morning (Sunday).

To exercise an abundance of caution, those who currently live, work or have visited the two ZIP codes since late August and are experiencing flu-like symptoms, such as fever, cough, or difficulty breathing, should contact a healthcare provider immediately.

Please note that Legionnaires’ disease is not contagious and can be treated with antibiotics when caught early.

data.title: Donald Trump is right: 'Whoever wins AI, wins' — no pause!
data.description:
As a variety of pundits from across the political spectrum make clear they desperately want to regulate AI, President Trump is holding the line. He announced the following yesterday:  

 “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades! The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’ like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’ – and we will continue to do so! We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies! There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so. Conspiracy Theorists, Treasonists, Traitors, and Leakers, BEWARE! Thank you for your attention to this matter! President DONALD J. TRUMP”  

Vice President Vance echoed those comments. 

On the other side, Democrats strongly believe more regulation is necessary — even existential. Here was Sen. Jon Ossoff.

That ex-Anthropic whistleblower he mentioned, Jacob Coxon, is joining forces with Bernie Sanders, and also Steve Bannon apparently. They will appear together at an ostensibly “pro human” AI event.  

And already, there are huge efforts underway to guilt Trump into going along. I saw reports yesterday that advisers in the White House are urging Trump to address the nation and promise some new wave of AI legislation. OpenAI’s Sam Altman is making his appeal based on Trump’s love of winning prizes, and says if Trump and Xi Jinping come together to safeguard AI, they should win the Nobel Peace Prize.  

Now this all sounds good in theory. Who is against sensible regulation to make sure AI superintelligence doesn’t pose a threat to humanity?  

In theory, no one. But when we get more specific than that, what Anthropic is asking for doesn’t really make sense: i.e., putting in limitations so these so-called frontier models have to advance slowly. A regulation to prevent swift advancement actually benefits whichever company is already winning, by making it impossible for some other AI competitor to catch up. That’s not fair — it’s regulatory capture, and it’s something that happens all the time, despite Rahm Emanuel’s contention that he’s unfamiliar with CEOs begging for regulation.  

The dominant market player is often interested in regulation! It happens all the time! They want to kneecap their competitors and remain in their position of dominance! That’s what matters most to Anthropic, believe you me.  

So what’s the remedy? Well, as former FTC commissioner Lina Khan points out, there are already laws on the books to punish companies from releasing defective products out onto the market. I never ever ever ever ever agree with Lina Khan, and I think she has a broad conception of consumer harm that ends up punishing large companies for making products that their consumers actually do want. But in this case she’s raising a valid point: Harm to the consumer is already the point of antitrust law, and if any AI company is flouting that, there can already be consequences. It’s perfectly fine to enforce that.  

And that’s basically what Trump was saying: Millions of Americans chose Trump to be their president in this moment because they trust his judgment. He seems to understand that we need to let AI companies compete with one another to offer useful new models, and that any company that does something hostile or intrinsically evil can face the necessary consequences. So based on that, I would recommend the AI doomers should chill out.  

Robby Soave is co-host of The Hill’s commentary show “Rising” and a senior editor for Reason Magazine. This column is an edited transcription of his daily commentary.

data.title: Top Oversight Democrat wants answers on Russian oligarch's role in Trump Jr.'s wedding
data.description:
Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.), the ranking member on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, pressed for answers on a Russian oligarch’s reported role in a wedding for one of President Trump’s sons.

According to a report published Monday by ProPublica, Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding in May received funding from Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev, who is linked to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The outlet reported that the oligarch paid for Trump Jr.’s wedding expenses in the hundreds of thousands of dollars, citing records and three sources with knowledge of the event. For the president’s son’s big event, ProPublica reported, Kremlev helped rent an island and put up the money for a fireworks show.

“Why did a Russian oligarch close to Putin fund Trump Jr.’s wedding in the Bahamas?” Garcia said in a Monday morning post on the social platform X, responding to the report.

“Umar Kremlev spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on the President’s son. What did he get in return? We need answers,” he added.

Last December, Trump Jr. said that he was engaged at the White House holiday party in front of family, friends and guests. The president’s son called his engagement to Bettina Anderson, a Palm Beach, Fla., socialite, a “big win” for the end of 2025.

Trump Jr.’s wife, who now goes by Bettina Trump, clapped back at the ProPublica report in an Instagram post on Monday, saying that she and her husband “got married privately on” May 22, “surrounded ONLY by our family.”

“Our dear friend Umar very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations for us AFTER our wedding. It was an extraordinarily generous wedding gift from a friend, and something for which we were and remain incredibly grateful,” she added later.

The Hill has reached out to Kremlev for comment.

data.title: Trump says Russia, Ukraine agree to avoid energy targets as fuel prices rise
data.description:
President Trump said Monday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to avoid energy targets in their ongoing war as global fuel prices rise.

“Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy targets. Russia has agreed to do likewise!” Trump said in a post on Truth Social.

The post comes as both gasoline and diesel prices are rising worldwide. Refining capacity shortages are a factor in the high prices, as global conflicts take out refineries. 

U.S. diesel prices recently crossed $6 per gallon for the first time ever, and averaged $6.23 per gallon on Monday, according to AAA. Gas prices averaged about $4.32 per gallon.

The high prices have created issues for the White House going into the midterms. Trump, in his post, sought to distance his administration and its decision to go to war with Iran from the issue. 

“The World’s Diesel price rise is mostly caused by the Russia/Ukraine War, not Iran,” he said. 

Experts have said that the Russia-Ukraine conflict is playing a part, but it’s not the only thing driving up prices, as Middle East instability is also factor.

“Average gasoline and diesel prices rose in every state over the last week as geopolitical tensions escalated on multiple fronts, with friction between the U.S. and Iran, new hostilities in the Red Sea, and the shutdown of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline all combining to jolt prices sharply higher,” said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy in a statement posted online. “New weekend attacks also knocked two additional Russian refineries offline, further straining global refined product supplies and likely offsetting any seasonal relief.”

data.title: How to fix NATO's fatal flaw
data.description:
For longer than I can remember, pleading with NATO to address what has been and is now a more obvious fatal flaw has not yielded a single action. That flaw is that its bedrock Article Five commitment that “an armed attack against one NATO member shall be considered an attack against them all,” presumes the attack will be a military assault by the Soviet Union on one or more members of the alliance.

But what if the attack is not military? The only precedent is when Article Five was invoked 25 years ago after al Qaeda’s strike on New York’s Twin Towers — when the alliance went to war in Afghanistan.

Vladimir Putin is using what Lenin termed “active measures” and what the West calls “hybrid warfare” in attacking NATO and Western countries. Russia is using active measures, including spreading as much chaos as possible short of an armed attack, in its plan to divide and fracture the alliance. And much like Lenin, who recruited useful idiots to his service, Putin has done the same with President Trump. Trump has gone out of his way to strain America’s links with NATO by demanding that NATO Europe take more responsibility for its defense — but “more” means “all” in Trump talk.

From 2003 to 2016 I served on the advisory board for a series of NATO’s Supreme allied commanders in Europe. During the years since, trying to get NATO to respond and react to these active measures has proved to be Sisyphean. NATO, to its credit, has created 30 wide-ranging Centers of Excellence that cover cyber, counterintelligence and strategic communications. But none focuses on dealing with active measures.

NATO has not confronted determining when active measures or hybrid warfare attacks trigger Article Five. Russia’s use of drones is an example. Sixteen NATO members have reported Russian drones penetrating national air space. Romania has cited 26 such violations, and this past August, shot down four Russian drones.  On Aug. 4, a Russian drone attack took place at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Germany. Fortunately it failed to explode.

The cyber realm is another area that Russia exploits regularly. The exact number of cyber attacks Russia is making against NATO is difficult to determine, but it is a very large number.  The most infamous of these was the Internet Research Agency in St. Petersburg, which founded by Yevgeny Prigozhin, who also headed the Wagner Group until his killing in 2023.

Russia has a number of these so-called troll offices that deal with the disinformation aspects of war and have been highly effective in spreading dissent among NATO and Western states. Yet so far, NATO has not taken collective action to counter these propaganda machines, leaving it up to individual member states to react.

What then should NATO do to protect and defend against Russian and possibly Chinese active measures and hybrid war? This question can raise intractable issues as to what might invoke Article Five, so it has been deferred. Since cyber responses involve highly classified national capabilities that can be shared, for example among the Five Eyes coalition of the U.S., United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and New Zealand, they usually do not apply across all of NATO’s 32 members.

First, NATO should state that any Russian drones penetrating its nations’ territorial air or waters will be destroyed. NATO can expand its air policing to that end. Expanding cybersecurity and infrastructure protection must be a high priority. And expanding strategic communications to counter Russian propaganda and disinformation must take place.

Second, NATO should use its exercises and deployments as part of influence operations against the Russians to match or expose active measures. As a further example, Putin is reportedly upset when a Tomahawk shooter is in range of him. That might be an interesting pressure point to exploit.

Third, under the Supreme Allied Commander Europe, NATO should create what Churchill called in World War II, a “dirty tricks” organization. Best described under a benign name such as special services, this organization would be tasked to take on and blunt Russian active measures and hybrid war.

Having offered these proposals before, perhaps this time round, someone may listen.

Harlan Ullman is senior adviser at Washington’s Atlantic Council, chairman of a private company and principal author of the doctrine of shock and awe. His next book, co-written with Field Marshal The Lord David Richards, former UK chief of defense and due out this fall, is “Who Thinks Best Wins: How Decisive Strategic Thinking Will Prevent Global Chaos.“

data.title: AI leaders call for development slowdown
data.description:
A growing chorus of artificial intelligence leaders are calling for a slowdown of the technology’s development following a researcher’s ominous warning that AI could soon destroy humanity.

Shortly after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called to slow down AI capability development, several of his competitors, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI CEO Elon Musk, followed suit.

The calls followed a post from 27-year-old AI researcher Jacob Coxon, who claimed researchers at the firms “believe AI could kill all humans” but still push forward in a race to develop superintelligence — a hypothetical AI agent that outperforms all of humanity’s cognitive performance. Coxon resigned from Anthropic before sharing his warnings on social media.

In a lengthy post on X, Altman said the world “world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened.”

“Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot,” Altman said.

Altman reiterated OpenAI’s support of a federal framework for safety requirements, but also argued the industry does not need to wait for legislation or an antitrust exemption to create “consistent rules” and shared values along the firms.

Altman said pacing development does not mean stopping, but that development “should be slower than it otherwise could be.”

“Pacing will be well worth this cost; no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring,” Altman said.

Musk, who originally co-founded OpenAI with Altman, reposted Amodei as well, writing that “Dario is right.”

The comments mark a shift for AI leaders, who have shied away from any commitments to slow down until recently.

Researchers have warned of AI’s potential danger for years, but nothing struck a chord quite like Coxon’s social media thread.

Coxon’s assessment went viral with more than 165 million views and within a few hours, the debate over the long-term implications of artificial intelligence was no longer confined within the technology community. 

Coxon is among a camp of what critics dubbed AI “doomers,” who believe the technology will lead to mass extinction if development is not safety-aligned or slowed down. 

“These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources,” Coxon wrote on social media. “We have all witnessed the progress in each of these domains, and progress is not slowing.”

Evan Hubinger, Anthropic’s head of alignment science, affirmed Coxon’s warning, stating, “Jacob is correct here—we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!”

data.title: Watch live: Vance, Blanche unveil fraud charges tied to COVID-era emergency loans
data.description:
Vice President Vance and Attorney General Todd Blanche are expected to unveil new fraud charges on Monday tied to Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA) loans issued during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The announcement in Kansas City, Mo., comes as the Trump administration continues its efforts to crack down on alleged fraud. Small Business Administration chief Kelly Loeffler, FBI Director Kash Patel and other federal, state and local officials will also be in attendance.

The press conference is scheduled to begin at 12:15 p.m. EDT.

data.title: ICE has no plans to 'sweep polling locations' for noncitizens, Homan says
data.description:
White House border czar Tom Homan on Sunday said there are no plans in place for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers to “sweep polling locations” in the November midterm elections.

Homan told Fox News host Jacqui Heinrich on “The Sunday Briefing” that he has not seen “any operational plans or any discussions on any immigration enforcement operation at polling places,” when Heinreich asked if there was any truth to claims that ICE will be “raiding” polling locations.

“This is another fear tactic. This is another attack on ICE and this administration,” Homan said about the claims. “I mean, they don’t want ICE near the polling places, they don’t want to vote for voter ID, they don’t want observers. What have they got to hide to begin with, right? But there is no plan for enforcement action at polling places. It’s just another attempt to smear ICE and smear the president.”

Homan also pushed back on reports of ICE arrests at elementary schools, hospitals and places of worship, saying there’s no “sensitive location” policy.

“If you’re a criminal alien, you’re a national security threat, there’s no sanctuary,” he said. “But look at the past two years. Not one instance of ICE operating at a sensitive location, [including] polling places.”

Latino civil rights and voting rights groups, along with the city of Denver, last week filed a lawsuit to block ICE from polling locations. The plaintiffs cited post-Civil War-era federal laws barring armed federal personnel at polling locations to prevent the intimidation of voters.

Lawyers for Denver and other plaintiffs — which include immigrant rights groups League of United Latin American Citizens, Common Cause and UnidosUS — wrote, “the specter of armed officers at polling places threatens the freedom of this upcoming election.”

“It places voters in fear that they will be confronted by armed federal immigration enforcement officers if they choose to cast a ballot,” they added.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said earlier this month that ICE would appear at polling places if there is a threat or a warrant for “someone that we have been actively tracking down.” He made similar remarks in an interview with CNN’s Kasie Hunt in June, noting that ICE would not be at polling locations because “only people that should be voting there is American citizens.”

Democratic lawmakers have slammed any notion of armed ICE officers operating at polling locations, echoing the lawsuit in suggesting their presence amounts to voter intimidation.

The Department of Justice has plans to deploy monitors to voting sites this November. The Trump administration has also sought to pursue restrictions on mail-in voting and creating voter lists alongside the added security.

data.title: Trump defends AI approach, criticizes Anthropic CEO and 'conspiracy theorists'
data.description:
President Trump defended his approach to Artificial Intelligence Monday, saying the only protections needed are a “STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT” amid calls for AI guardrails.

“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” he wrote on Truth Social. “The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things.’”

“We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies!” he continued. “There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China.”

Trump wrote that U.S. is “leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so.”

“Conspiracy Theorists, Treasonists, Traitors, and Leakers, BEWARE!” he wrote.

He specifically named Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei as an example of someone who has done “bad,” but said he is “now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel.’”

Amodei has recently said AI development should slow down to allow for guardrails to be implemented.

“To be clear, pacing does not mean halting model training or technical progress, but ensuring companies take adequate time to align and safeguard their models, and for third party evaluators to confirm this,” Amodei wrote in a blog post over the weekend. “Our pacing framework is an attempt to further strengthen our commitment to safety and encourage a race to the top.”

The president has repeatedly downplayed calls for an AI slowdown and more guardrails from industry leaders and those across the political aisle.

“We can put guardrails, we can do this and that, but I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up that … shouldn’t be bringing it up, and they’re bringing up things that won’t happen,” Trump told reporters over the weekend.

Trump and his allies argue that the U.S. must win the AI race against China.

“I said it from the very beginning….whoever wins AI wins,” he said.

But the public and lawmakers in both parties appear to be growing more concerned about AI. Their worries run the gamut from how AI could affect the economy and eliminate jobs, to its potential threats to humanity.

Senate Democratic Leader Charles Schumer (N.Y.) on Monday called for a classified briefing on the dangers of AI.

Lawmakers in both parties also have raised concerns about AI data centers, which Trump has repeatedly defended.
